label: prose:sm-results-index
title: Location and status of the Standard-Model results
html:
The framework's Standard-Model results are not confined to this appendix. They are distributed across several chapters, and the two strongest are not stated here at all. This section is the index; it moves no material, because each block is correctly placed for its own chapter's argument, and relocating them would create backward edges elsewhere. What was missing was a way to find them.

What is derived

Three items, corpus-wide. Everything else on this surface is standard representation theory, a machine-checked negative, a precise identification without a derivation, or open.

Result Where Status
Coulomb charge Q = w/2, and I_3 on the nucleon doublet Coulomb charge, gauge truncation derived; the per-crossing coupling c = 1/2 is structurally fixed, not fitted
Weak isospin T_3 = \mathrm{sign}(\kappa)/2 as a grading orthogonal to the generation winding QOU/ParticleInteractions/WeakIsospinT3Grading.lean derived from an oriented crossing already in the corpus; closes Gell-Mann–Nishijima
\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} to 0.313 parts per billion under the proton pin QOU/AlphaEM/FormLadderAnchorDominance.lean, alpha-em-form-ladder.witness.json partial: three unproved classes remain, and the anchor choice constitutes the residual

Scope on the first of these: the I_3 identification is a two-point sign-and-ratio match on the proton–neutron doublet. It matches sign and ratio, scale-free; it does not make I_3 an output for general states.

Where the rest is

Eleven blocks outside this appendix carry Standard-Model or flavour content, across five chapters, together with Lean and compute that no chapter surfaces.

Chapter Carries
nuclear-interactions the categorical Weinberg angle
mass-theory the complex-mass constituent functional; the flavour-split Habiro derivation
knots-particles-confinement the electroweak torus-link triplet; the involution pair
observations the CP-violation survey
eightfold-way the multiplet classification and its null results

Unsurfaced elsewhere: WeakIsospinT3Grading.lean, MesonOperatorSelectionT3.lean, FormLadderAnchorDominance.lean, the \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} form ladder, and the stage-1 quark-mass extraction scoping.

The dominant mode of contribution is deletion

A reader asking what these derivations give should be told this first. The surface carries five self-withdrawals and several machine-checked negatives against one derived entry, and the negatives are worth more. Gell-Mann–Okubo, the decuplet equal-spacing rule behind the \Omega^- prediction, and the Coleman–Glashow relation are each proved to hold identically for any first-order octet breaking. Reproducing them is therefore evidence for nothing, and removing them as derivation targets is a larger contribution than most positive results would have been, because it stops a zero-information success from being counted as one.

The testable content is what remains: their deviations, respectively about 6\%, 9.2\% and 0.8\%. The framework derives no second-order term, so it predicts zero for all three.
